original_findings: Required correction in reasoning_map.joins[node=N4].why_each. It says the hull endpoints certify ‘a positive final amplitude’ at every enumerated cut. The endpoint amplitude can be negative. In the provided example the component left of the cut (1,2) has only −3/5 as a nonzero target entry. Replace the premise with ‘a nonzero target amplitude on the side away from s, hence positive target squared mass there’ (or equivalently ‘positive final mass’). The zero-side argument excludes either sign. Re-hash and compare the corrected full payload while retaining this original digest and finding.
revision_history.prior_text: The cut invariant describes what omitting an edge enforces. The endpoints of the hull certify that a positive final amplitude violates that invariant at every enumerated cut.
revision_history.corrected_text: Omitting the cut edge keeps the side away from the source at zero squared mass. An endpoint of the hull on that side has a nonzero target amplitude of either sign, giving the side strictly positive target squared mass and forcing a gate across this cut.
revision_history.resolution: Accepted on the revised full bytes. For each L≤k<R, a hull endpoint on the side opposite s is in the target support, so that side has strictly positive target mass even if all its nonzero amplitudes are negative. In the printed example, cut (1,2) has 9/25 final mass on its initially empty left side from −3/5 at site 1; cut (4,5) has 16/25 on its initially empty right side from +4/5 at site 6. Both force a crossing. A field-by-field comparison found no other payload difference.

items.semantic_core_verdict: The fixed-span projection/Cauchy–Schwarz subproof is shared with the T3 comparator in the frozen plan. The objective here additionally requires a causal characterization over arbitrary tree circuits, a schedule-preserving signed synthesis, and a polynomial optimum over child-to-time matchings. These distinguish its mathematical task from fixed-subspace projection, depth counts for a supplied sequence and static edge coloring within the screened concepts.
items.reasoning: The monotone marked set covers support even if a rotation acts on zeros, revisits an edge or cancels an amplitude. Connectedness on a tree makes the predecessor the unique parent, and disjoint layer edges prevent same-slot relay. The upper bound for a schedule is the norm squared of the coordinate projection. To attain it for a positive-weight nonsingleton I, reverse its first-contact layers and fold each signed (parent,child) pair to (ρ,0). Child transmissions occur after the child's own receipt in forward time, hence before its parent fold in reverse. Zero pairs are fixed by identity; a last root merge leaves +1. Inverting gives the normalized signed target restriction in the available layers. Negative a_r on a singleton reached set is handled at the score level, and zero mass never requires normalization. Distinct contact slots j for children leave t−j layers. Overlaying sibling subtree schedules after those slots cannot conflict with a parent transmission. Thus F(v,t)=a_v²+max_M ΣF(u,t−j), F(v,0)=a_v², and F(r,d) is the maximum score. The table and each assignment instance have polynomial sizes in n,d+1. The example gives 0,1/2,1; the authored circuit puts the negative sign on the last transfer to v′, while my Phase I circuit put it on the previous transfer into v. Both are legal in parent-child order. At depth two there is a single first root transmission, so it is impossible to capture both distance-two leaves.
